decisions.claim: B showed or presented A with a Hello Kitty item dressed in a monkey suit
decisions.reason: A's 'Yeah, it's really cute' and direct questions about 'a monkey suit' on 'Hello Kitty' presuppose that B brought this item to A's attention (showed, presented, or shared it). The 'Yeah' signals agreement with or reaction to something B introduced.
decisions.counterexample: They could be looking at a shared screen or shop display together without B specifically 'showing' it to A, but the conversational structure still implies B initiated the topic.

decisions.claim: A asked B whether B was born in the year of the monkey
decisions.reason: This claim describes an action performed by A (asking a question), not an attribute of B. Questions do not establish their answers. A's inquiry about B's birth year does not confirm B was born in the year of the monkey, nor does it constitute a B-attribute.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply 'No, I was born in the year of the dragon' and A's question remains fully consistent with all visible turns.

decisions.claim: B responded to A's inquiry with something that A dismissed with 'Not at all'
decisions.reason: This claim describes B's act of responding, which is an unseen turn. We cannot infer what B said from A's 'Not at all!' alone. The claim attributes a communicative action to B that is not recoverable from A's visible turns.
decisions.counterexample: B could have said 'No, I wasn't born in the year of the monkey' or 'I don't know' or any other reply; 'Not at all' is consistent with multiple different B responses.

design: dual route, targeted rescue, globally grouped evidence adjudication
